key_insight: Frozen world models for Atari Pong still make obvious visual and dynamical mistakes, and concept-guided spatial regularization can partially reduce those failures.
engineering_relevance: For model-based RL systems, evaluating the world model itself—not just end-policy return—can reveal brittle predictive errors that directly limit downstream performance.
method: Reproduced and trained five visual world models: DreamerV3, DIAMOND, TWISTER, Simulus, and STORM.
Ran closed-loop rollout diagnostics with separately trained policies interacting with frozen world models.
Added Concept-Guided Spatial Regularization (CGSReg), an auxiliary pixel reconstruction loss over segmented concept regions.
evidence_signal: Across all five models, rollouts showed failures such as ball disappearance, wrong ball motion, and invalid paddle interactions, and zero-shot pixel-space MBRL underperformed the original pipelines, with DreamerV3 dropping from -5.5 to -20.9 mean return.
watch_item: CGSReg improves some models and metrics but does not eliminate all world-model bottlenecks, so gains may be model- and task-dependent.
paper_title: Concept-Guided Spatial Regularization for World Models in Atari Pong
